title: fix(cli): os meta delete says nothing was deleted when the reset door answers reset: false
body:
Fixes #23479
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`os meta delete`'s default (human) output now reads the reset door's `reset` flag. The `--format json` and `--format yaml` outputs already report that flag as `deleted`. Until now the human output printed its success line without reading it.

`packages/cli/src/commands/meta/delete.ts`, `run()`'s human branch:

- `reset: false` means the delete's address held no row, so nothing was removed. In that case the command prints a warning line, built from the flags it sent:

| Run | Before | Now |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `os meta delete view x`, nothing stored | `✓ Metadata deleted: view/x` | `⚠ Nothing deleted: view/x — the server found nothing to delete` |
| `... --package P`, P holds no row of it | `✓ Metadata deleted: view/x` | `⚠ Nothing deleted: package 'P' holds no row of view/x` |
| `... --draft`, no pending draft | `✓ Pending draft discarded: view/x` | `⚠ Nothing discarded: view/x has no pending draft` |
| `... --draft --package P`, P holds no pending draft of it | `✓ Pending draft discarded: view/x` | `⚠ Nothing discarded: package 'P' holds no pending draft of view/x` |

- `reset: true`: the success line is unchanged, byte for byte, including with `--package`.
- The flag is read as `=== false`, not as falsiness. `false` is the door's positive "nothing was removed" (`DeleteMetaItemResponseSchema`). An absent flag carries no signal, and reading it as "nothing deleted" would deny a deletion that really happened. The sibling `os data delete` reads its flag the same way (#19413).
- Each no-op sentence claims only what the door's own no-op receipt claims for that address (`ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.deleteMetaItem`'s `reset: false` returns). With `--package P`, the door's receipt is "No row of TYPE/NAME is bound to package 'P', so nothing was deleted", and on `--draft` it is "No pending draft of TYPE/NAME is bound to package 'P'". The command names no cause it did not read: it does not say "already at artifact default", and it does not say which package holds the row instead. The package id is quoted verbatim, as it was sent.

## The no-op exit code: measured, unchanged (`0`)

The command already declares a no-op as a completed command that exits `0`:

- Its JSON and YAML outputs publish `success: true` (the CLI envelope's "the command completed") beside `deleted: false`. The `[#13023]` note in `run()` defines the two booleans that way.
- `delete-reset-carriers.test.ts` already pins two real-door no-ops at exit `0`: "NAMING A PACKAGE THAT HOLDS NO ROW" (`--format json`, `deleted: false`) and "`--draft` parses" (a `--draft` reset of `view/nothing_here`).
- Measured on the new head through the real door (probe below): the human output also exits `0` on all five no-op runs.
- Neither the command's docblock nor `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` declares a different code for `os meta delete`. `cli.mdx` has no `os meta delete` entry.

So the exit code stays `0` on both values and all three formats. Moving only the human output off `0` would re-create the disagreement one layer down. Moving all three would narrow a published CLI accept set, so it is not done here. The sibling `os data delete` made the same call for the same reason (#19413). Failures (a refusal or a transport error) still exit `1`, and the pin file has a control for that.

## Pins: `packages/cli/src/commands/meta/delete-noop-line.test.ts` (unit tier)

The pins drive the real oclif command and a real `ObjectStackClient` whose `fetch` returns a canned receipt from the door. The receipts use the shapes and sentences of the door's own delete and no-op returns. There are four argv variants: no flag, `--package`, `--draft`, and `--draft --package`.

- **POSITIVE CONTROL:** both receipts reach the command through the real SDK verbatim, with `reset` intact.
- **`reset: true`:** each variant's whole output equals its success line, and the exit code is `0`. *Negative control:* no `Nothing deleted` or `Nothing discarded` text appears.
- **`reset: false`:** each variant's whole output equals its no-op line, and the exit code is `0`. *Negative control:* no `Metadata deleted`, no `Pending draft discarded`, and no success glyph.
- **`--package P` names P, verbatim, and only P.** *Negative control:* the package-less no-op line names no package.
- **All three formats state the same fact:** JSON `deleted`, YAML `deleted`, and the human line agree for every variant and both values. `humanClaim` refuses an output that says neither sentence, or both.
- **Exit code `0`** on both values × three formats × four variants. *Control:* a 500 from the transport still exits `1`.

### Ablation (one-off, not kept)

The fix was committed first. Then `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` mutated the anchor `if (result.reset === false) {` to `if (false) {`, which restores the unconditional success line. It ran the pin file in WRAP mode under the verify lock:

```
ablation-replace: anchor   x1 -> x0
ablation-replace: replace  "if (false) {"  x0 -> x1
ablation-replace: blob     291bceebf307... -> 16421ba34632...
 ✓ POSITIVE CONTROL — both receipts reach the command through the REAL SDK, verbatim
 ✓ `reset: true` — the success line, byte for byte, on every variant
 × `reset: false` — the no-op line, and NOT the success line
     + "out": "  ✓ Metadata deleted: view/nothing_here",
 × `--package P` names P, verbatim, and only on the no-op line
 × all three arms state the SAME fact, for one and the same receipt
 ✓ the exit code is `0` on BOTH values and all three formats
 ✓ a genuine transport failure still exits 1
 Tests  3 failed | 4 passed (7)
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (291bceebf307) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

The direction is red, as predicted. The three cases that read the `reset: false` branch go red. The four that do not (the control, the `reset: true` pin, the exit-code pin and the transport control) stay green. The subject is imported relatively (`./delete.js`, from `src`), so no `dist/` rebuild was involved.

### Real-door probe (one-off, not kept)

This is the card's two repros plus the draft no-op and a delete-ful control. They ran through the real `RestServer`, `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` and SQLite `sys_metadata`, using the harness from `delete-reset-carriers.test.ts`, on head `c52520177f`:

```
PROBE nothing_here:                "  ⚠ Nothing deleted: view/nothing_here — the server found nothing to delete" exit 0
PROBE nothing_here json:           { "success": true, "type": "view", "name": "nothing_here", "deleted": false } exit 0
PROBE --package gamma:             "  ⚠ Nothing deleted: package 'com.qa.gamma' holds no row of view/probe_v" exit 0
PROBE --package gamma json:        { "success": true, "type": "view", "name": "probe_v", "deleted": false } exit 0
PROBE --package none stored:       "  ⚠ Nothing deleted: package 'com.qa.gamma' holds no row of view/probe_none" exit 0
PROBE --draft none:                "  ⚠ Nothing discarded: view/probe_d has no pending draft" exit 0
PROBE --draft --package none:      "  ⚠ Nothing discarded: package 'com.qa.gamma' holds no pending draft of view/probe_d" exit 0
PROBE control:                     "  ✓ Metadata deleted: view/probe_ok" exit 0
```

In the same run, `delete-reset-carriers.test.ts` (integration tier, real door) was green: 2 files, 34 tests.

## Verification

All of the following ran on head `41060487d3`, after the final commit. The code has not changed since the ablation and the probe, which ran on `c52520177f`. Exit codes were captured before any pipe. Heavy runs went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

- **Build:** `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/cli^...' --concurrency=2` built the dependency closure (VERDICT command-exit 0). A full `pnpm turbo run build --filter='!@objectstack/docs' --concurrency=2` followed (VERDICT command-exit 0, 75/75 tasks), because the dist-reading gates and two CLI pins need every package built.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0.** The new pin file is in that `tsc` program: `tsc --listFilesOnly -p tsconfig.json` lists `src/commands/meta/delete-noop-line.test.ts`, and `check:test-typecheck` reports its debt ledger held.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`:** 288 of 290 files and 4295 tests passed (29 skipped). The 2 failed files were `test/published-subpath-console.pin.test.ts` and `test/published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts`. Both refused at load with "packages/cli is not built (./dist/index.js is absent)", a prerequisite and not a finding. They were re-run after the full build: 2 files and 29 tests passed (exit 0). The `integration` tier is declared to CI. Locally I ran only `delete-reset-carriers.test.ts` from it, in the probe run above: green, 2 files and 34 tests.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 64 commands, and all 64 were run. Four refused on the first pass with exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, unbuilt dist): `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage` and `check:i18n-walk-parity`. After the full build they were re-run with exit 0. `check:dts-closure`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:published-files` and `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` were also re-run on the built tree: exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: "64 derived, 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN" (a derived zero; every line carries its exit code).
- **`pnpm lint`** (the whole-repo `eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0, no findings.
- **Control-byte self-scan** of the three changed files: no matches.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not surfaced on any output: the door's `message`.** The no-op receipt carries a sentence that names what remains, for example "package 'com.qa.alpha' still holds a row". The JSON and YAML outputs drop it too (`{ success, type, name, deleted }`). Surfacing it would be a new output key or line, which is outside this card. This is an observation, not filed.
- **The legacy raw-engine path (read-only inference, not exercised).** On a control-plane kernel, for a code-only type, the door's legacy branch matches the row by type, name and organization only. It does not read `state` or `packageId`. So a `--draft` or `--package` reset there would remove whatever row it finds, and the CLI would print the `--draft` success line. This is dormant: it is not reached from an environment kernel, and draft or packaged rows of `job` or `agent` are not writable. It is not filed, and is noted here for the reset-door owner.
- The new pin file is unit tier (it imports no driver and constructs no `ObjectQL`). The integration-tier `delete-reset-carriers.test.ts` is untouched; its success-line assertions are `reset: true` runs and still hold.
